gates.name: Coverage policy
gates.pass_condition: overall statement >=90%/branch >=85%; core statement >=95%/branch >=90% per quality/convergence.json.coverage; loop/scripts/check_coverage.py reads those four thresholds from that document and asserts each dimension separately against the coverage json report, exiting non-zero and naming every dimension below its floor; the two qt_controller_* thresholds are reported as an explicit SKIP until ADR-0001's PySide6 migration makes them measurable
gates.note: owned by WI-000 (control-plane tooling, REQ-028); coverage runs via the authoritative unittest runner, not pytest (the legacy Tk GUI suite is flaky under pytest — see loop/quality/TOOLCHAIN_BASELINE.md). Enabled 2026-07-16 at 5906cf0 on freshly measured evidence: all four documented thresholds now pass — overall stmt 92.99/90, branch 87.84/85; core stmt 99.75/95, branch 99.26/90 (values recorded in quality/convergence.json.coverage.current), after the two test-strengthening rounds 209c19b and 5906cf0 took the suite from 467 to 580 tests. The former `coverage report --fail-under=85` step was replaced by loop/scripts/check_coverage.py because --fail-under floors only coverage.py's combined statement+branch total: on 2026-07-15 that blended 86.8% passed while all four documented thresholds failed, so the gate would have certified a green it never checked. Coverage omits ui/_app_members.py (ADR-0014 type-only base for pyright, never imported at runtime; its 310 declarations are unexecutable and uncoverable by any test, and counting them distorted the total to 82.7%).

gates.name: Security and export safety
gates.pass_condition: TEST-SEC-001 passes: every CSV/clipboard export neutralizes the =/+/-/@ (and TAB/CR) formula-injection leads. The dependency-scan half of the original condition ('0 critical/high') is vacuous for the shipped artifact and is not asserted here -- see note; re-add a scan command the moment a runtime dependency is introduced.
gates.note: Enabled 2026-07-16 with the REQ-032 defence it was always meant to guard. Until then the gate was an empty placeholder (commands:[]) that could neither pass nor fail, and the defence it named did not exist: exports wrote "=cmd|' /C calc'!A0" verbatim into CSV, so Excel/WPS evaluated it (DDE). Owner moved WI-018 -> WI-028 to match the export-security split. Two halves of the old pass_condition are deliberately NOT asserted, rather than faked: (1) '0 critical/high' -- the product declares zero runtime dependencies and the EXE bundles only the stdlib, so there is no third-party surface to scan; this becomes real the moment a runtime dependency (e.g. PySide6 per ADR-0001) lands. (2) path traversal -- no path is derived from data anywhere (CSV path comes from the OS save dialog, config from %APPDATA% plus a fixed filename, assets from code constants), so there is no surface to defend.
